notes: Retrieval was badly poisoned: 'filter' and 'sanitize' in these corpora overwhelmingly mean data-cleaning ETL chores, not security filter bypass, and I discarded almost the entire lexical shortlist. The real TB2.1 skill is offensive: craft one input that survives a text-based HTML sanitizer yet still executes JS, which hinges on the gap between the filter's HTML parsing and the browser's. TMax is the only pool with true offensive payload-crafting tasks (forge XSS/HTML, evade an IDS, bypass a validator) and carries the final top 10. SWE-Smith contributes the exact HTML-sanitizer library domain (bleach, markupsafe, mistune, readability) but as bug-fixes, so it loses hard on task_form. SWE-Rebench's markdown-1072 is a standout: its entire discussion is the parser-discrepancy reasoning that mXSS bypasses rely on. Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld have no HTML/XSS security tasks, so I mapped them to their nearest cousins (SQL/command injection, JWT forgery, crackme/exploit payload crafting); their scores reflect real but weaker transfer.
